verifications.claim: The Go Blue Guarantee is a University of Michigan program providing free or reduced tuition for up to four years to in-state, full-time undergraduate students with a family income of $125,000 or less and assets below $125,000.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "All three U-M campuses offer the Go Blue Guarantee — free and reduced tuition for up to four years for qualified high-achieving, in-state, full-time undergraduate students." "Michigan families with incomes $125,000 and under & assets below $125,000 now qualify for FREE TUITION." "Family income $125,000 or less Assets below $125,000" "To receive the Go Blue Guarantee, an individual must be a Michigan resident... enroll in full-time study... meet the income and asset criteria."
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the program details matching the claim exactly, including campuses, duration, in-state full-time undergrads, and income/asset thresholds.

verifications.claim: The Go Blue Guarantee applies to the Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Flint campuses.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "All three U-M campuses offer the Go Blue Guarantee" "Ann Arbor Dearborn Flint"
verifications.reasoning: R4 explicitly names all three campuses as offering the program.

verifications.claim: The Go Blue Guarantee covers tuition and mandatory fees for qualified students.

verifications.reasoning: R9 directly confirms coverage of tuition and mandatory fees; R4 supports free tuition.

verifications.claim: "Go Blue" originated in the 1950s (or possibly late 1940s) as a rallying cry, according to The University Record.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "History does not paint a clear, definite picture of how “Go Blue” became the rallying cry... coined in the 1950s... spring of 1947." From record.umich.edu.
verifications.reasoning: R2 from The University Record directly attributes origins to 1950s or 1947 as rallying cry.

verifications.claim: Various accounts attribute the popularization of "Go Blue" to student fans at hockey and football games, according to The University Record.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "attended a varsity hockey game... shouting “Go Blue!”... home football opener against Michigan State... invented and introduced the “Go Blue” cheer at a U-M baseball game." From The University Record.
verifications.reasoning: R2 describes multiple accounts including hockey and football games.
